_about: The fixture drug registry: a dozen medicines common in Malaysia and Singapore, shaped like the NPRA and HSA registers with a licensed monograph beside each. Registration numbers are shaped like real ones and are not real ones. This file is the only source of pharmacology in the tests and on a dev run; nothing in app/ writes drug facts from anywhere else. Monographs carry rule ids, not prose: the sentences live in app/medicines/strings.py. Grown to a real sample of at least 200 MY/SG products (E00-06): the original dozen stay exactly as they were; every product after them is new, across the common community-pharmacy and chronic-disease list — cardiovascular, diabetes, lipids, analgesia, gastro, respiratory — plus the supplements and TCM remedies patients take beside them (E04-03), all screened for interactions the same way a prescription medicine is; `product_kind` says which is which. An interaction's `source` is what a pharmacist would check it against; `review_state` is `awaiting_review` for a pair not yet checked by one — still flagged, never silent, queued for the pharmacist review queue (`app.language.review`) the first time it is actually raised for a person.
